title: Deposit Terms Applying to Booked Events — Private Event & Banquet Services
content:
Deposits on Private Event & Banquet Services are taken in up to two instalments against the estimated contracted value of the event, at the percentages printed against the package.

## When each instalment falls due

The first deposit is due no later than the deposit due window for the package, counted in calendar days from the day the booking is confirmed. Calendar days are counted from the day after the booking is confirmed, every day of the week counts, and a deposit paid on the boundary day itself is in time; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods. The day the booking was confirmed is taken from the booking entry standing in the agreement's event ledger, and the comparison is made before the deposit is taken.

The second deposit, where the package carries one, is due the number of calendar days before the event printed against the package, and a package whose second deposit percentage is zero takes no second deposit however large the event.

### Boundary cases on a hypothetical due window of 10 days

| The booking was confirmed on | Deposit paid on | In time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The confirmation day | The tenth day after it | Yes, the boundary day itself is in time |
| The confirmation day | The eleventh day after it | No |

Counting begins on the day after confirmation, so a deposit paid on the confirmation day itself is also in time, and a weekend day between the two is counted like any other day.

## Where the first deposit is not paid

A booking whose first deposit is not paid by the due day is released from the diary and the date offered to other clients, and the client is told before the date is released.

## When deposits are returnable

Deposits are returnable in full where written notice of cancellation reaches Larkspur Table more than the refundable window printed against the package before the event date, and are not returnable at all inside that window, where they are set against the cancellation charge instead. Where the deposit held exceeds the cancellation charge, the difference is returned to the client rather than held on account.

## The states in which a deposit is taken or returned

A deposit is only taken or returned on an agreement that stands active or on hold, since a closed agreement holds no diary and a proposed agreement carries no bookings. That state is read from the company's records against the agreement's own reference before the money moves, together with the deposit money the records show standing on it.
